reasons: The candidate multiplies by a constant 100 that does not appear in the Datadog source, which the hard rules forbid. A unit scale must be proposed in notes, not applied in promql.

The Datadog metric nginx.net.request_per_s is already a per-second rate. Mapping it to rate(nginx.requests[$__rate_interval]) is a reasonable quantity match, but the candidate adds the unsupported scale on top of it.

The Host template variable has prefix host and default *, so it should become host=~"$Host". The candidate drops it, which changes the set of series. The dataset does not list a host label among observed labels, so this needs checking against the dataset.
Aggregation avg() across series matches the Datadog avg, and there is no grouping in either query, so those aspects are consistent.
